source: Five additional user photographs of the Passaporte para Português glossary, main pages 143, 145, 147, 149 and 151 plus readable preceding-page fragments
normalization_notes: Visual transcription of every readable Portuguese glossary row on main pages 143, 145, 147, 149 and 151, plus readable preceding-page fragments. No inferred words from unphotographed pages.
Source references, book titles and page numbers are JSON metadata only, not categories or CEFR levels.
Lowercase NFC-normalize and remove punctuation; discard trailing gender articles but retain articles and prepositions within phrases.
Expand mau/má into mau and má. Separate se from mudar-se. Retain lexical compounds mal-educado, meia-noite, meio-dia, norte-americano, quarta-feira and quinta-feira.
Keep actual contextual components such as cabelo, carne and exame; preserve phrases in extracted JSON and translate each imported word independently.
Keep conjugated words puxe, queria and quer, feminine adjectives fotográfica and marcada, and plural melhoras; do not invent additional lemmas.
Preserve Portuguese diacritics: pais and país, por and pôr, porque and porquê, and mau and má are distinct word forms.
Retain loiça as printed; do not silently replace it with the alternate spelling louça.
Keep all repeated source senses for mala, mulher and quadro while deduplicating word records.
Pai Natal and meia de leite are split exactly as printed. Capitalized Papa and Natal are lowercased for the database, with source capitalization preserved here.

enrichment.translations: English/Ukrainian translations for new words supplied by the assistant. Existing translations preserved exactly. Photographed German glosses retained in extracted JSON.
enrichment.levels: A1/A2 estimates by the assistant for new words; not source-provided levels. Existing CEFR labels preserved.
enrichment.groups: Only existing topic and grammatical categories; no provenance categories.

dictionary_checks.note: Verified both US/American and broader North American senses; both are retained in translations.

translation_notes: Puxe is pull, the formal imperative of puxar; it is not English push.
Papa is lowercased for the database but translated as pope, following the photographed capitalized noun, not the homograph for porridge.
Pais means parents and país means country; neither accents nor lexical hyphens are discarded.
Medicina denotes the medical field; medicamento is the separate word for a medicinal drug.
Natural is translated independently as natural; the full água natural phrase and German gloss remain in source context.
Quer is a form of querer meaning wants; the phrase quer dizer means means, and is not copied as the standalone translation of quer.
Existing mulher and planta already cover both photographed senses; existing translations are retained.
Meia de leite, máquina de lavar loiça, Pai Natal and other expressions remain in JSON as expressions while only their constituent words are imported.
The database still contains individual words only; new entries start at mastery 0 and old records/history are preserved.
